what_its_for: Modafinil helps you stay awake if you have excessive sleepiness caused by narcolepsy (a condition where you fall asleep suddenly), sleep apnea (where breathing stops during sleep), or shift work sleep disorder (trouble staying awake during work hours due to an irregular schedule). It does not cure these conditions, but it helps reduce daytime sleepiness.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. If you are taking it for narcolepsy or sleep apnea, take it in the morning. If you take it for shift work, take it about 1 hour before your work shift begins. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not crush or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 200 mg once a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well it works for you and how you tolerate it. Do not take more than your prescribed dose. Do not take a second dose in the same day unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still daytime and you need to be awake. If it is already close to your bedtime or you no longer need to stay awake, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store modafinil at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store it in a secure place out of the reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking modafinil, as it can make side effects worse and affect your judgment. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, since it can sometimes cause dizziness or blurred vision. Avoid taking it late in the day or at night, as it may make it hard for you to fall asleep. Modafinil can make hormonal birth control (pills, patches, rings, implants) less effective — use an additional form of birth control (such as condoms) during treatment and for one month after stopping. Limit caffeine, as combining it with modafinil may increase nervousness or a racing heart.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you develop a skin rash, hives, blisters, peeling skin, or sores in your mouth — these can be signs of a serious and rare skin reaction. Also call your doctor if you experience chest pain, an irregular heartbeat, trouble breathing, severe anxiety, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), unusual changes in mood or behavior, signs of allergic reaction (swelling of the face, lips, or throat), or if your sleepiness does not improve with treatment.
when_it_works: Modafinil starts working within 1 to 2 hours after you take it. Most people notice improved wakefulness on the first day of treatment. However, it may take a few days to find the best dose for you. Remember, it helps manage your sleepiness but does not replace good sleep habits or treat the underlying cause of your condition.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): The dose may need to be lower because the medication stays in the body longer as we age. Kidney or liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, your doctor will likely prescribe a lower dose. People with heart problems: Tell your doctor if you have a history of heart disease, heart attack, or irregular heartbeat before starting this medication. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: The safety of modafinil during pregnancy is not well established. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Modafinil is not approved for use in children and teenagers under 17 years of age.
